title: MCP conformance trace event
description: One record of an MCP conformance trace. A trace is a JSON Lines document: one event object per line, no blank lines, no byte-order mark, `seq` strictly increasing in document order. Line-level rules are outside JSON Schema and are enforced by the reader (mcp-trace-validator's `reader::parse_trace`), as is one type rule: `seq` and `status` must be written without a fractional part (`1`, not `1.0`), which JSON Schema's `integer` does not distinguish. Unknown members are ignored, so producers may add their own.

seq.description: Capture-assigned sequence number: the only ordering authority within the trace.

transport.description: The transport the session ran over.

kind.description: Which of the three event shapes this is.

ts.description: Informational timestamp (RFC 3339). No check reads it.

capture.description: What the recorder says it left out of the trace, as of the moment it closed it. Written by a recorder that reports it, on the closing lifecycle event (`kind` `lifecycle`) only; read from a lifecycle event only. The recorder's own statement, which nothing authenticates, and no verdict depends on it. A trace without one says nothing about what was left out.

unrecorded.description: What the session carried that is not in the trace, counted by kind. The kinds are the recorder's own names (`mcp-trace-capture` writes `oversized`, `over_budget` and `other_events`); a reader must accept a kind it does not know. A kind that did not occur is left out, so an empty object reports that nothing was.

then.description: A JSON-RPC message, exactly as captured.

method.description: The request method, when the event records a client request: the token as the request carried it, compared exactly (RFC 9110 section 9.1 makes it case-sensitive), so `post` is not `POST`.

status.description: The response status, when the event records a response.

headers.description: Recorded headers. Names are read case-insensitively; credential-bearing headers should not be recorded.
